adversarial.description: Evaluator-originated name-driven bypass probe (methodology/02 Sec 8; not among the contract's 14 verification items or the 92 contract-review mutants, which use only ordinary directory names), run by the replayable helper .agent/evidence/105-qa-adversarial-helpers/special_name_probe.py. The claim map is bash keyed by directory name (claim_count["${entry}"], claimed_dir["${f%%/*}"]); in bash the subscripts '@' and '*' are special even for associative arrays (they expand to all values), so a directory literally named '@' or '*' could have been read as claimed whenever any real claim exists. For each hostile name the helper copies the repository (symlinks preserved) into a private directory outside the repository, creates tools/fixtures/<name>/probe.json, runs bash tools/fixtures_self_test.sh there, and requires exit 1, a 'SELF-TEST FAILED' line and the name reported as an unclaimed subdirectory. Names: an ordinary control, a hidden dot directory, a space, a leading dash, '*', '@', 'a]b' and '$(echo hi)'; an unmodified copy is the positive control (exit 0, 'SELF-TEST OK: 146/146').
adversarial.result: PASS (exit 0, problems: []). The positive control passed (146/146) and all eight hostile or control names made the guard exit 1 with 'SELF-TEST FAILED' and the name reported as an unclaimed subdirectory; no name evaded the claim map. Scratch copies were removed and the real tree was not written.
